```{r setup, echo=FALSE}
# setwd("~/Documents/Experiment")
# getwd()

#load packages
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#load datasets
summary_data <- read_csv("experiment_summary.csv")
frame_data <- read_csv("experiment_data.csv")

# Create contribution-angle factor

summary_data <- summary_data %>%
  mutate(
    contribution_angle = as.factor(target_angle)
  )

# Check data
names(summary_data)
names(frame_data)
```

```{r}
# 1. Remove practice trials 
summary_clean <- summary_data %>%
  filter(mode != "practice")

table(summary_clean$mode)
```
```{r}
#remove noemi
summary_clean <- summary_data %>%
  filter(!(participant_id == "noemi" & mode == "individual")) %>%
  filter(!(dyad_id == "jens_noemi" & mode == "cooperative"))
```

```{r}
# Check trial counts 
summary_clean %>%
  count(mode, phase)
```

Each trial produced two rows in the dataset (one for the approach phase and one for the homing-in phase). The individual, playback, and AI conditions were completed by individual participants and therefore contained up to 480 observations per phase, while the cooperative condition contained 240 observations per phase because the analysis was based on 12 dyads.

```{r}
# Set contribution-angle order
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    contribution_angle = factor(
      contribution_angle,
      levels = c("0", "22.5", "45", "67.5", "90")
    )
  )
```


```{r}
# 2. Removing the pretarget measurements
frame_clean <- frame_data %>%
  filter(phase != "pre_target")

# Check
table(frame_clean$phase)
```

```{r}
# 3. Define and label error trials in the dataset

# In Wahn et al. (2016), error trials were defined as trials in which the cursor entered the homing-in zone but then exited it again, or moved outside the screen boundaries. -> In our experiment, error trials were defined as trials in which the cursor exited the homing-in zone after entering it, failed to maintain stable target contact for the required dwell time, or moved outside the screen boundaries. The addition of the dwell-time criterion reflects our requirement that participants stabilise the cursor on the target rather than only reaching it momentarily.

summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(error_trial = FALSE)

# Check 
table(summary_clean$error_trial)

# After applying the operational definition to the dataset, no trials were classified as error trials in the sample. 
```

```{r}
# 4. Label conditions (making it factor variable)
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    condition = factor(
      mode,
      levels = c("individual", "cooperative", "playback", "ai")
    )
  )

table(summary_clean$condition)
```

```{r}
# 5. Label higher-level partner/adaptiveness type
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    partner_type = case_when(
      condition == "individual" ~ "no_partner",
      condition == "cooperative" ~ "adaptive_human",
      condition == "ai" ~ "adaptive_ai",
      condition == "playback" ~ "nonadaptive_playback"
    )
  )

# Convert it to a factor 
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    partner_type = factor(
      partner_type,
      levels = c(
        "no_partner",
        "adaptive_human",
        "adaptive_ai",
        "nonadaptive_playback"
      )
    )
  )

# Check 
table(summary_clean$partner_type)
```

```{r}
# 6. Converting phase to factor variable 
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    phase = factor(
      phase,
      levels = c("approach", "homing_in"),
      labels = c("Approach", "Homing-in")
    )
  )

# Check
table(summary_clean$phase)
```

```{r}
# 7. Check contribution angles
table(summary_clean$contribution_angle)
```

```{r}
# 8. Making sure iteration is numeric for further analysis 
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    iteration = as.numeric(iteration)
  )

# Check
glimpse(summary_clean)
```

```{r}
# 9. Add axis-control variable
frame_clean <- frame_clean %>%
  mutate(
    axis_control = case_when(
      
      # AI condition
      mode == "ai" & ai_axis == 1 ~ "AI_vertical",
      mode == "ai" & ai_axis == 0 ~ "AI_horizontal",
      
      # Playback condition
      mode == "playback" & playback_axis == "vertical" ~ "Playback_vertical",
      mode == "playback" & playback_axis == "horizontal" ~ "Playback_horizontal",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Convert to factor
frame_clean <- frame_clean %>%
  mutate(
    axis_control = factor(axis_control)
  )

# Check
table(frame_clean$axis_control, useNA = "ifany")
```

```{r}
# 10. Use logged dyad ID
summary_clean <- summary_clean %>%
  mutate(
    dyad_id = as.character(dyad_id),
    dyad_id = na_if(dyad_id, ""),
    dyad_id = factor(dyad_id)

# Check
table(summary_clean$dyad_id, useNA = "ifany")
```

```{r}
# 11. Create trial-level dataset
trial_data <- summary_clean %>%
  select(
    participant_id,
    dyad_id,
    mode,
    condition,
    partner_type,
    iteration,
    phase,
    target_angle,
    contribution_angle,
    reaction_time_s,
    distance_px,
    error_trial
  )

# Check
trial_data %>%
  count(condition, phase)

#This trial_data will be the main dataset for: RT analyses; DIST analyses; ANOVAs; t-tests; condition comparisons and learning analyses.
```

```{r}
# 12. Rename dependent variables for analysis
trial_data <- trial_data %>%
  rename(
    RT   = reaction_time_s,
    DIST = distance_px
  )

# Check
glimpse(trial_data)
```

```{r}
# 13. Remove error trials from RT/DIST analyses
analysis_data <- trial_data %>%
  filter(error_trial == FALSE)

# Check
table(analysis_data$error_trial)
```
Error-trial criteria: "Two types of behavior were classified as errors: If the cursor moved into the homing-in zone but then excited it again, and if the cursor moved outside of the screen borders." (Wahn at al., 2016)

```{r}
# 18. Calculate collective benefit (RT)

# Mean individual RT per participant
individual_RT <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "individual") %>%
  group_by(participant_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    individual_RT = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Mean cooperative RT per dyad
cooperative_RT <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "cooperative") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    cooperative_RT = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Best individual within each dyad
#dyad mapping
participant_dyad_map <- tibble::tribble(
  ~participant_id, ~dyad_id,
   "666",         "666_����",
   "����",      "666_����",
   "august",      "august_jens",
   "jens",        "august_jens",
   "jakob",       "jakob_niels",
   "niels",       "jakob_niels",
   "odin",        "odin_line",
   "line",        "odin_line",
   "valeria",     "valeria_emil",
   "emil",        "valeria_emil",
   "lasse",       "mads_lasse",
   "mads",        "mads_lasse"
  
)

best_individual_RT <- individual_RT %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    best_individual_RT = min(individual_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate collective benefit
collective_benefit_RT <- cooperative_RT %>%
  left_join(
    best_individual_RT,
    by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    collective_benefit = best_individual_RT / cooperative_RT
  )

# Check
glimpse(collective_benefit_RT)
```
```{r}
#Collective benefit DIST

individual_DIST <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "individual") %>%
  group_by(participant_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    individual_DIST = mean(DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cooperative_DIST <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(condition == "cooperative") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    cooperative_DIST = mean(DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#Best (lowest) individual DIST within each dyad
best_individual_DIST <- individual_DIST %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    best_individual_DIST = min(individual_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#collective benefit (DIST)
collective_benefit_DIST <- cooperative_DIST %>%
  left_join(
    best_individual_DIST,
    by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    collective_benefit = best_individual_DIST / cooperative_DIST
  )

#check
glimpse(collective_benefit_DIST)


```
Collective benefit interpretation: "Values above 1 indicate a collective benefit because dyad RT is lower than the faster member's RT. This measure was calculated separately for Approach and Homing-in phase - averaged across all contribution angles as well as separately for each of the three contribution angles (30%, 50%, 70%)"
- 0° and 90°: only one dyad member controls controls the cursor as only horizontal or vertical is required
- 45°: both members contributed equally - 50%
- 22.5° and 67.5°: one of the members contributed more than the other: 30% vs 70%

```{r}
# 19. Calculate skill ratio (RT)
skill_ratio_RT <- individual_RT %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    faster_partner = min(individual_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    slower_partner = max(individual_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    skill_ratio    = faster_partner / slower_partner,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# Check
glimpse(skill_ratio_RT)
```

```{r}
#Skill ratio DIST
skill_ratio_DIST <- individual_DIST %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    faster_partner = min(individual_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    slower_partner = max(individual_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    skill_ratio    = faster_partner / slower_partner,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# Check
glimpse(skill_ratio_DIST)
```
Skill ratio interpretation: A value of 1 indicates that both members perform equally well individually, whereas an increasingly lower ratio indicates a larger interindividual performance difference.

#INDIVIDUAL and COLLECTIVE analysis

```{r}
#correlating interindivual RT skill ratios with collective benefit for each of the contribution conditions, separately for Approach and Homing-in

#join the two into one data frame
corr_data <- collective_benefit_RT %>%
  left_join(skill_ratio_RT, by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle"))

#Pearson r between skill_ratio and collective benefit
correlation_results <- corr_data %>%
  group_by(phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(skill_ratio) & !is.na(collective_benefit)),
    r = cor(skill_ratio, collective_benefit, use = "complete.obs"),
    p_value = tryCatch(
      cor.test(skill_ratio, collective_benefit)$p.value,
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      p_value < .001 ~ "***",
      p_value < .01  ~ "**",
      p_value < .05  ~ "*",
      p_value < .10  ~ "†",
      TRUE           ~ ""
    )
  )
print(correlation_results)

#plot
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(corr_data, aes(x = skill_ratio, y = collective_benefit)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.75, aes(colour = phase)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  facet_grid(phase ~ contribution_angle,
             labeller = labeller(
               contribution_angle = function(x) paste0(x, "°")
             )) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Approach" = "#4C9BE8", "Homing-in" = "#E8834C")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Skill ratio RT vs. collective benefit RT",
    subtitle = "Rows = phase  |  Columns = contribution angle",
    x        = "Skill ratio (best RT / worst RT)",
    y        = "Collective benefit (best individual RT / cooperative RT)",
    colour   = "Phase"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

```{r}
    ),

  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  facet_grid(phase ~ contribution_angle,
             labeller = labeller(
               contribution_angle = function(x) paste0(x, "°")
             )) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Approach" = "#4C9BE8", "Homing-in" = "#E8834C")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Skill ratio DIST vs. collective benefit DIST",
    subtitle = "Rows = phase  |  Columns = contribution angle",
    x        = "Skill ratio (best DIST / worst DIST)",
    y        = "Collective benefit (best individual DIST / cooperative DIST)",

  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
Interpretation: Wahn et al. predicted that the collective benefit systematically increases with larger skill ratios, suggesting that dyad members who have increasingly similar individual performance levels benefit more from performing jointly - particularly when both members contribute equally to the joint performance. If however the better individual's dominance compensates for a larger interindividual difference (as in the 70% contribution condition (22.5° and 67.5°)), they predicted a reduced correlation relative to the other contribution conditions.
- With only 6 dyads, we have very low power per angle x phase cell, so we have to trat the correlations as descriptive/exploratory and flag that in the write-up (we could collapse across angles and just group by phase for more statistical power, but I don't think we should)

```{r}
#Checking for social facilitation
#Comparing RT in the individual and joint condition for the baseline angles 0° and 90°
#done separately for Approach and Homing-in

library(effectsize)

#filter to baseline angles
temp_sf <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(contribution_angle %in% c(0, 90),
         condition %in% c("individual", "cooperative")) %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(dyad_id = coalesce(dyad_id.x, dyad_id.y)) %>%
  select(-dyad_id.x, -dyad_id.y)

social_fac_data <- temp_sf %>%
  group_by(participant_id, dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_RT = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#summary table
social_fac_summary <- social_fac_data %>%
  group_by(phase, contribution_angle, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n     = n(),
    M_RT  = mean(mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_RT = sd(mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(social_fac_summary)

#paired t-tests + Wilcoxon + Cohen's d per phase x angle

#individual: average both members per dyad
temp_ind <- social_fac_data %>%
  filter(condition == "individual") %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(dyad_id = coalesce(dyad_id.x, dyad_id.y)) %>%
  select(-dyad_id.x, -dyad_id.y)

individual_sf <- temp_ind %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(ind_RT = mean(mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#cooperative
cooperative_sf <- social_fac_data %>%
  filter(condition == "cooperative") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(coop_RT = mean(mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#join and run both t-test and Wilcoxon with Cohen's d
sf_tests <- individual_sf %>%
  left_join(cooperative_sf, by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")) %>%
  group_by(phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    n         = n(),
    M_ind     = mean(ind_RT,  na.rm = TRUE),
    M_coop    = mean(coop_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_diff = mean(coop_RT - ind_RT, na.rm = TRUE),
    t_stat    = tryCatch(t.test(coop_RT, ind_RT, paired = TRUE)$statistic,  error = function(e) NA),
    t_p_value = tryCatch(t.test(coop_RT, ind_RT, paired = TRUE)$p.value,    error = function(e) NA),
    W_stat    = tryCatch(wilcox.test(coop_RT, ind_RT, paired = TRUE)$statistic, error = function(e) NA),
    W_p_value = tryCatch(wilcox.test(coop_RT, ind_RT, paired = TRUE)$p.value,   error = function(e) NA),
    cohens_d  = tryCatch(
      repeated_measures_d(coop_RT, ind_RT, method = "z")$d,
      error = function(e) NA
    ),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    t_sig = case_when(
      t_p_value < .001 ~ "***",
      t_p_value < .01  ~ "**",
      t_p_value < .05  ~ "*",
      t_p_value < .10  ~ "†",
      TRUE             ~ ""
    ),
    W_sig = case_when(
      W_p_value < .001 ~ "***",
      W_p_value < .01  ~ "**",
      W_p_value < .05  ~ "*",
      W_p_value < .10  ~ "†",
      TRUE             ~ ""
    )
  )
print(sf_tests)

#plot
temp_plot <- social_fac_data %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(dyad_id = coalesce(dyad_id.x, dyad_id.y)) %>%
  select(-dyad_id.x, -dyad_id.y)

temp_plot %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle, condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_RT = mean(mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(contribution_angle = factor(paste0(contribution_angle, "°"),
                                     levels = c("0°", "90°"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = condition, y = mean_RT, colour = condition, group = dyad_id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line",
               linewidth = 1.2, colour = "grey20") +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "point",
               size = 4, shape = 18, colour = "grey20") +
  facet_grid(phase ~ contribution_angle) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("individual"  = "#4C9BE8",
                                 "cooperative" = "#E8834C")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("individual"  = "Individual",
                               "cooperative" = "Cooperative")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Social facilitation check",
    subtitle = "Baseline angles only  |  Rows = phase  |  Columns = angle",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Mean RT (s)",
    colour   = "Condition"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
Interpretation:

1. Approach phase: At 0°, there was no significant difference between individual and cooperative RT (W = 11, p = 1.000, d = 0.12). Similarly, at 90°, cooperative and individual RTs did not differ significantly (W = 9, p = .844, d = -0.19), with the small negative d indicating cooperative RT was marginally faster than individual.

2. Homing-in phase: At 0°, no significant difference was found between conditions (W = 13, p = .688, d = 0.05). At 90°, cooperative RT (M = 5.24 s) was notably slower than individual RT (M = 2.78 s), though this difference did not reach significance (W = 17, p = .219, d = 0.53), representing a medium effect size.

```{r}
#Checking for social facilitation
#Comparing DIST in the individual and joint condition for the baseline angles 0° and 90°
#done separately for Approach and Homing-in

library(effectsize)

#filter to baseline angles
temp_sf_dist <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(contribution_angle %in% c(0, 90),
         condition %in% c("individual", "cooperative")) %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(dyad_id = coalesce(dyad_id.x, dyad_id.y)) %>%
  select(-dyad_id.x, -dyad_id.y)

social_fac_data_dist <- temp_sf_dist %>%
  group_by(participant_id, dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_DIST = mean(DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#summary table
social_fac_summary_dist <- social_fac_data_dist %>%
  group_by(phase, contribution_angle, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n       = n(),
    M_DIST  = mean(mean_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_DIST = sd(mean_DIST, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(social_fac_summary_dist)

#paired t-tests + Wilcoxon + Cohen's d per phase x angle

#individual: average both members per dyad
temp_ind_dist <- social_fac_data_dist %>%
  filter(condition == "individual") %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(dyad_id = coalesce(dyad_id.x, dyad_id.y)) %>%
  select(-dyad_id.x, -dyad_id.y)

individual_sf_dist <- temp_ind_dist %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(ind_DIST = mean(mean_DIST, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#cooperative
cooperative_sf_dist <- social_fac_data_dist %>%
  filter(condition == "cooperative") %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(coop_DIST = mean(mean_DIST, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#join and run both t-test and Wilcoxon with Cohen's d
sf_tests_dist <- individual_sf_dist %>%
  left_join(cooperative_sf_dist, by = c("dyad_id", "phase", "contribution_angle")) %>%
  group_by(phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(
    n         = n(),
    M_ind     = mean(ind_DIST,  na.rm = TRUE),
    M_coop    = mean(coop_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_diff = mean(coop_DIST - ind_DIST, na.rm = TRUE),
    t_stat    = tryCatch(t.test(coop_DIST, ind_DIST, paired = TRUE)$statistic,      error = function(e) NA),
    t_p_value = tryCatch(t.test(coop_DIST, ind_DIST, paired = TRUE)$p.value,        error = function(e) NA),
    W_stat    = tryCatch(wilcox.test(coop_DIST, ind_DIST, paired = TRUE)$statistic, error = function(e) NA),
    W_p_value = tryCatch(wilcox.test(coop_DIST, ind_DIST, paired = TRUE)$p.value,   error = function(e) NA),
    cohens_d  = tryCatch(
      repeated_measures_d(coop_DIST, ind_DIST, method = "z")$d,
      error = function(e) NA
    ),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    t_sig = case_when(
      t_p_value < .001 ~ "***",
      t_p_value < .01  ~ "**",
      t_p_value < .05  ~ "*",
      t_p_value < .10  ~ "†",
      TRUE             ~ ""
    ),
    W_sig = case_when(
      W_p_value < .001 ~ "***",
      W_p_value < .01  ~ "**",
      W_p_value < .05  ~ "*",
      W_p_value < .10  ~ "†",
      TRUE             ~ ""
    )
  )
print(sf_tests_dist)

#plot
temp_plot_dist <- social_fac_data_dist %>%
  left_join(participant_dyad_map, by = "participant_id") %>%
  mutate(dyad_id = coalesce(dyad_id.x, dyad_id.y)) %>%
  select(-dyad_id.x, -dyad_id.y)

temp_plot_dist %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle, condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_DIST = mean(mean_DIST, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(contribution_angle = factor(paste0(contribution_angle, "°"),
                                     levels = c("0°", "90°"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = condition, y = mean_DIST, colour = condition, group = dyad_id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line",
               linewidth = 1.2, colour = "grey20") +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "point",
               size = 4, shape = 18, colour = "grey20") +
  facet_grid(phase ~ contribution_angle) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("individual"  = "#4C9BE8",
                                 "cooperative" = "#E8834C")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("individual"  = "Individual",
                               "cooperative" = "Cooperative")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Social facilitation check (DIST)",
    subtitle = "Baseline angles only  |  Rows = phase  |  Columns = angle",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Mean DIST",
    colour   = "Condition"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
Interpretation:

1. Approach: At 0°, dyads travelled slightly more distance cooperatively (M = 326) than individually (M = 305), a mean difference of 20.4 units, though this was non-significant (W = 11, p = .418, d = 0.42). At 90°, a similar pattern emerged — cooperative DIST (M = 330) exceeded individual DIST (M = 303) by 26.9 units, again non-significant (W = 9, p = .787, d = 0.30). Both effects are small-to-medium in size but in the direction of a coordination cost — dyads travel more than individuals.

2. Homing-in: At 0°, the pattern reverses: cooperative DIST (M = 300) was actually lower than individual DIST (M = 377), a mean difference of -76.6 units (W = 9, p = .844, d = -0.25). This hints at a slight collective benefit in path efficiency, though it is non-significant and small. At 90°, the largest effect emerges — cooperative DIST (M = 448) was 238 units greater than individual DIST (M = 209), a medium effect (d = 0.48) that nonetheless failed to reach significance (W = 18, p = .156), suggesting a meaningful coordination cost at maximal asymmetry during Homing-in.

```{r}
#2x3 Repeated measures ANOVA: phase x contribution angle
#at contribution angles
#separately for RT and DIST

library(ez)
library(effectsize)

#RT

anova_data_RT <- collective_benefit_RT %>%
  filter(contribution_angle %in% c(22.5, 45, 67.5)) %>%
  mutate(
    phase               = factor(phase),
    contribution_angle  = factor(contribution_angle)
  )

#check for missing cells
anova_data_RT %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, phase, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  print()

#ANOVA
anova_RT <- ezANOVA(
  data       = anova_data_RT,
  dv         = collective_benefit,
  wid        = dyad_id,
  within     = .(phase, contribution_angle),
  type       = 3,
  detailed   = TRUE,
  return_aov = TRUE
)
print(anova_RT)

#effect sizes (partial eta squared is given by ezANOVA,
# but also compute Cohen's f for completeness)
effectsize::eta_squared(anova_RT$aov, partial = TRUE)

#post-hoc pairwise comparisons if contribution_angle is significant
#collapsed across phase
pairwise_RT_data <- anova_data_RT %>%
  group_by(dyad_id, contribution_angle) %>%
  summarise(mean_benefit = mean(collective_benefit, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

pairwise_RT <- pairwise.t.test(
  x               = pairwise_RT_data$mean_benefit,
  g               = pairwise_RT_data$contribution_angle,
  paired          = TRUE,
  p.adjust.method = "bonferroni"
)
print(pairwise_RT)
```

```{r}
#Steiger test for comparing correlations between angles both DIST and RT
library(cocor)

run_steiger <- function(corr_data, correlation_results, measure_label) {
  
  angles <- c(22.5, 45, 67.5)
  phases <- c("Approach", "Homing-in")
  
  # all pairs where 67.5° is compared to the other two
  comparisons <- list(
    c(67.5, 22.5),
    c(67.5, 45)
  )
  
  for (phase_label in phases) {
    
    d <- corr_data %>% filter(phase == phase_label)
    
    r_vals <- correlation_results %>%
      filter(phase == phase_label) %>%
      select(contribution_angle, r) %>%
      deframe()
    
    n <- d %>%
      filter(contribution_angle == angles[1]) %>%
      summarise(n = sum(!is.na(skill_ratio) & !is.na(collective_benefit))) %>%
      pull(n)
    
    get_r <- function(a1, a2) {
      x <- d %>% filter(contribution_angle == a1) %>% pull(collective_benefit)
      y <- d %>% filter(contribution_angle == a2) %>% pull(collective_benefit)
      cor(x, y, use = "complete.obs")
    }
    
    for (pair in comparisons) {
      a1 <- pair[1]; a2 <- pair[2]
      cat("\n======", measure_label, "|", phase_label, ":", a1, "° vs", a2, "° ======\n")
      print(cocor.dep.groups.overlap(
        r.jk = r_vals[as.character(a1)],
        r.jh = r_vals[as.character(a2)],
        r.kh = get_r(a1, a2),
        n    = n
      ))
    }
  }
}

#RT
run_steiger(corr_data, correlation_results, "RT")

#DIST
run_steiger(corr_data2, correlation_results2, "DIST")
```
